posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hello all,

These are final corrections of Quiz 1 Paper sent for signoff.

  • Sleep and Coproc Question → Both the coproc and sleep 5m & are valid ways of sleeping for 5 minutes in the background. However, & itself is a statement terminator and thus we do not need ; after it. In fact, &; would cause a syntax error, making the option technically incorrect. Many of you have marked only coproc (25\%). Although this option was put to test if the student knows that sleep supports time units such as m, h etc, as it is technically incorrect due to ;, we shall be giving marks for everyone who attempted this question.

  • Find Question → Here the only obvious answer is the one with -not -name. However it is not correct due to multiple reasons.

  1. We should quote the *, otherwise it will be expanded as a file glob by bash instead. This will only work correctly if there are no files in cwd, or there is only a single .txt file in cwd. In the first case the glob will not be expanded, and the second case the glob will be expanded to the filename of that txt file, and find will be called with -name test.txt (for example). Which is not the correct thing to do, but output will be correct. However, if there are more than one .txt file in the cwd, this will simply error out, as bash will expand the glob into multiple file names and give to find. To fix this we should have quoted the * like '*'.
  2. present in the current directory does not infer recursing into the child directories as well, so we should also put a -maxdepth 1 in the correct solution, or clarify whether to recurse in the question.
  3. count of files, and not directories, hence we should have a -type f
  4. Finally, this is not a big deal, but the “home directory of user user1” can technically be anywhere, not just /home/user1, that is the default location, not the only location. For example, refer the home location of root user. So as we are already in that location, we should simply use . instead of /home/user1
    Additionally, you could have also used ~user1, which is a shell shorthand which expands to the home directory path of user user1.
    Refer below example to understand it better:
    Screenshot 2025-02-26 at 12.20.58 PM802×296 98.4 KB

Due to several glaring mistakes in the correct option, we are marking it free for all who attempted this question, even though 97\% of you already marked the correct option.

  • Regex matching for hex code. Here the question mentions (extended), however the options are using BRE instead. However it was pretty clear what the options and question meant, and most of you (99.3\%) have marked the correct option(s). Thus there will be no change in this question.

TL;DR: find -not -now question and sleep 5m &; questions will receive full marks for anyone who has attempted.

Thank you for your patience, sorry for the discrepancies in the paper.

Edit: the stats used in this post are of the top 10\% performers. For the rest, the distribution is similar but skewed with a right tail.

Regards,
System Commands Team
